articles.title: Annotations
articles.summary: Draw on ChordPro and PDF songs in Songivo with Apple Pencil or touch, including Snap highlight for ChordPro.
articles.content: Markups Annotations Annotations let you mark charts on top of the song content. Use annotations for rehearsal marks, reminders, highlights, and personal performance cues. Annotation example. Draw on a song Open a ChordPro or PDF song. Turn on annotation mode. Use Apple Pencil or touch to draw, highlight, or erase. Use undo and redo while reviewing marks. Long-press a Pencil tool to change the annotation’s width and opacity. Tap Done before using performance gestures again. Use Snap highlight Snap highlight is available for ChordPro songs. When it is on, Songivo reads the highlighter stroke as a text selection and stores the highlight against matching chord or lyric fragments. That keeps highlights aligned when font size, columns, zoom, or device orientation changes. Turn on annotation mode. Keep Snap highlight enabled in the annotation toolbar. Use the highlighter across the lyric or chord text you want to mark. Use the eraser to remove individual marks. Clear All Drawings removes every annotation for the song. Snap mode while drawing. Snap mode after release. How annotations are saved PDF annotations are saved with the PDF song context. ChordPro annotations scale as content size changes. Band-song annotations stay private per user even when the shared song itself is common. Clear annotations only when you intend to remove saved marks for the active song context. Previous: Swiping Next: Band Libraries

articles.title: Band Libraries
articles.summary: Create, join, and manage Songivo band libraries with shared songs, setlists, members, invites, sync logs, and conflict review.
articles.content: Teams Band Libraries Band libraries keep songs and setlists separate from My Library and other band libraries, so collaboration does not overwrite material from another library. Use My Library for personal material and a band library for charts that should be shared with a band. Copy songs explicitly when they need to be available in another library. Band management starts in Settings, while library switching happens from the song and setlist panel. Create or join a band Open Settings and choose Band. Create a band when you are the leader, or join from an invite when another member created it. Select the band library before importing or copying shared songs. Use sync status and logs when shared changes do not appear yet. Confirm the active library before rehearsing so you do not edit a personal copy by mistake. The library switcher is the practical checkpoint before adding, importing, copying, or performing shared material. Shared library rules Band songs and setlists live in the selected band library. My Library and each band library remain independent. Songs move between libraries only through explicit copy actions. Leader-only deletion protects the shared band library from accidental removal. Band-song annotations stay private per user. Active band limits The free tier includes 5 active bands. Leaving or deleting a band frees an active band slot, and each €0.99 extra active-band purchase adds one more slot. Access to band libraries You can join and sync a shared band normally. When a shared band has more than 5 songs, its content requires a Yearly subscription or Lifetime unlock. This access rule is separate from the active-band limit; restore purchases or leave the band from the access prompt if needed. Conflicts Offline or concurrent shared edits can be marked “Conflict needs review.” Open the review flow and choose which local fields to keep versus the synced band version. Previous: Annotations Next: Gig Mode

articles.title: ChordPro
articles.summary: Use ChordPro songs in Songivo with directives, chords, sections, transposition, notation modes, and display settings.
articles.content: Charts ChordPro ChordPro songs give Songivo editable lyrics, chords, sections, metadata, transposition, and flexible stage layouts. Rendered ChordPro charts keep chords aligned with lyrics while still allowing font, layout, transpose, and performance controls. Edit a ChordPro song Open the song’s quick-actions menu and choose Edit Song. Update the required fields. Clean up the ChordPro source text with section directives and chord placement. Use linked songs when related charts should travel with the main song. Save and check the rendered chart before rehearsal. Edit metadata and source text in one place, then return to the viewer to confirm the rendered result. Transpose and notation Songivo can display transposed chords without rewriting the stored source text. Standard notation is best for common chord charts. Nashville notation supports number-based band workflows. Roman notation supports functional analysis and teaching contexts. Display options Use song and appearance settings to adjust font size, ChordPro layout mode, chord and lyric colors, column behavior, split-page behavior, and chord block alignment. Previous: Importing Songs Next: PDFs

articles.title: Exporting
articles.summary: Export Songivo songs, selected song PDFs, setlist summaries, and full set PDF packages.
articles.content: Share out Exporting Export options Export the current song as PDF when one chart is needed outside Songivo. Export selected songs (long press a song to go into multi-selection) into one combined PDF. Export setlist summaries as text. Export a set overview or a full combined set PDF package. Export a single song. Export the currently displayed song using the Export button. Export multiple songs. Export multiple songs. Export a set Open the setlist. Choose the export action. Select Full Set to export song content, or Set Overview to export only the set overview. Review the exported PDF before distributing it. Export sets. Previous: Gig Mode Next: Settings

articles.title: FAQ
articles.summary: Frequently asked questions about Songivo accounts, iCloud, band libraries, ChordPro, PDFs, exports, pricing, and supported devices.
articles.content: Reference FAQ Short answers to common Songivo setup, sync, library, pricing, and performance questions. Do I need a Songivo account? No. Songivo does not require a separate Songivo account for your personal library. Personal sync uses the Apple Account signed in to iCloud. What file types can I import? Songivo supports ChordPro, plain text, PDF, image, and SongBook Pro files, plus web search results from inside the app. Can I use Songivo without iCloud? You can use local app data on the device. iCloud is needed for personal sync between devices and sharing in a band. Are band libraries the same as My Library? No. My Library and each band library are independent. Copy songs explicitly when you want material in another library. Are my band annotations shared? The song remains shared while each player keeps personal markings. Why did importing a song use a free song addition? Song additions are counted when songs are created or imported. Deleting a song later does not restore that free addition. What devices are supported? Songivo is designed for iPhone and iPad on iOS/iPadOS 17 or later. What is included for free? The free tier includes 5 song additions, 5 active bands, and access to shared band libraries with up to 5 songs. How much does Songivo cost? Unlimited song additions and access to shared band libraries with more than 5 songs are available for €3.99 per year or a €14.99 lifetime unlock. Extra active band slots are €0.99 each, and each purchase adds one active band slot. Can I restore purchases? Restore Purchases restores yearly, lifetime, and eligible purchased extra active band slots for the same Apple Account. Is there a band member limit? Each band supports up to 25 invited members. The band leader is not counted as an invited member. Does the website track visitors? The Songivo website does not include analytics or tracking scripts. Previous: Troubleshooting Back to docs

articles.title: Getting Started
articles.summary: Start using Songivo on iPhone and iPad: open the library, import songs, edit charts, create setlists, and prepare for rehearsal.
articles.content: Start here Getting Started Songivo helps you access and manage your songbook. Start in My Library for personal songs. Use the song viewer for rehearsal, then add setlists, annotations, and performance tools as your library grows. The first screen gives you direct paths into browsing, creating, importing, settings, tuner, metronome, and live display controls. First useful setup Open the library and confirm the correct library context is selected. Start with the bundled demo songs or import one ChordPro, text, PDF, image, or SongBook Pro file. Open a song and check title, artist, key, BPM, duration, song number, and tags. Create a setlist when you need a rehearsal or show order instead of renaming songs. Open Settings once to review sync, appearance, editor fields, metronome, and purchase status. The library panel keeps songs searchable while the selected chart remains visible beside it on iPad. Main areas Library Search, filter, link alternate parts, copy, export, and open songs in the selected library. Viewer Read ChordPro or PDF charts with transpose, tuner, annotation, and live controls nearby. Setlists Build the order for rehearsal or a show, including slot notes and performance status. Settings Manage appearance, sync, band libraries, purchases, metronome sounds, and diagnostics. After you select a song, the viewer becomes the center of the workflow: read, edit, transpose, annotate, tune, or enter live mode. Good setup habits Add metadata early, especially artist, key, BPM, duration, song number, and tags. Keep My Library and band libraries separate unless you intentionally copy material between them. Use setlists for performance order instead of changing song titles for each event. Open important songs before the show to confirm font size, scroll speed, notes, and PDF zoom. Back to docs Next: Song Library

articles.title: Gig Mode
articles.summary: Use Songivo gig mode to push the active band song so listening devices switch to the matching local chart.
articles.content: Band stage Gig Mode Gig Mode lets eligible band members push the active song to listening bandmates. Gig mode belongs to a band workflow. Use song push Select the shared band library. Open the song that should be active for the group. Enable gig mode on devices that should listen. Push the current song from the leading device. Confirm listening devices switch to the matching local shared song. After a successful push, devices listening to the selected band switch to the matching shared song. The push control appears in the performance command area when the selected band supports gig mode and the current song can be pushed. What happens if a song is missing If a listening device does not have the pushed song locally, Songivo reports the missing song instead of switching blindly. Sync the band library and try again. Best use Use it during rehearsal or live mode when one person calls the next song. Keep the band library synced before the event. Confirm every device is using the same band context. Previous: Band Libraries Next: Exporting

articles.title: Importing Songs
articles.summary: Import ChordPro, text, PDF, image, SBP, web results into Songivo.
articles.content: Files and search Importing Songs Songivo imports local files and web search results into the currently selected library. Check the library context before importing. A song imported into My Library is personal; a song imported into a band library belongs to that shared band context. Use the import link to start importing new songs. Import from files Open Import Songs from the start screen, or library panel. Choose the File tab. Select one or more supported files. Review any preview, PDF processing, or duplicate prompt shown by Songivo. Save the imported songs and then adjust metadata such as key, BPM, duration, tags, and song number. Import files Import from web search Search by title or artist using the Web tab. Songivo searches its supported web sources automatically. Preview the result before importing so you can avoid a bad chart or a duplicate. Clean up metadata after import; web sources often need title, key, BPM, or formatting review. Import songs from web resources. Free song additions Creating or importing a song uses one free song addition until unlimited song additions are unlocked. Deleting a song later does not restore that free addition, so preview imports before saving. Previous: Link Songs Next: ChordPro

articles.title: Link Songs
articles.summary: Link related Songivo charts together for medleys, intros, reprises, alternate keys, and attached PDFs.
articles.content: Library Link Songs Linked songs keep related charts together while preserving each song as its own library item. Use links when a song needs more than one chart—for example, separate bass tabs or an intro. The song editor includes Linked Songs so you can manage linked charts without changing the main chart. Create a link Open the correct personal or band library. Swipe right on the chart you want to link. Tap Link, then choose the chart that should be the main song. Linking works best when each related chart is already cleanly named and easy to distinguish in the library. Library boundaries Links belong to the selected library context. Personal links and band-library links stay independent. A linked song cannot also be the main song of another linked group. Unlink a song when it should return to standalone performance navigation. Previous: Song Library Next: Importing Songs

articles.title: Live Performance
articles.summary: Use Songivo live mode, live bar controls, auto-scroll, tap tempo, tuner access, gestures, and keyboard shortcuts.
articles.content: Performance Live Performance The live bar keeps auto-scroll, scroll speed, the metronome, full-screen, and setlist status within reach during a performance. Use the live bar Adjust zoom, font size, and page layout (scroll vs. multi-page). Use the live bar to start auto-scroll, adjust its speed, and start or stop the metronome. Use the full-screen control to hide viewer controls during performance. Live-bar controls for auto-scroll, scroll speed, and the metronome. Previous: Setlists Next: Tuner & Metronome

articles.title: PDFs
articles.summary: Use PDFs in Songivo for lead sheets, scanned charts, import preview, page cleanup, annotations, and live performance.
articles.content: Scans PDFs Use PDFs for lead sheets, scanned charts, and documents where the original page layout should stay fixed. PDFs follow the same library rules as ChordPro songs: import into the selected library, check the preview, and verify readability before the show. Prepare a PDF Import the PDF into the correct personal or band library. Review the preview before saving. Rotate pages that were scanned sideways. Crop or correct perspective when a page was photographed. Apply contrast, grayscale, or optimization presets when readability improves. PDF import view. When to choose ChordPro instead Choose ChordPro when you need editable lyrics, transposition, notation changes, or flexible text layout. Choose PDF when the original page layout is the source of truth. Previous: ChordPro Next: Setlists

articles.title: Setlists
articles.summary: Create and manage Songivo setlists with performance dates, slot notes, reordering, performance status, and exports.
articles.content: Shows Setlists Setlists turn your library into the order you need for rehearsal, worship, theater, lessons, or a gig. A setlist stores performance order separately from the library. The same song can appear in many setlists without duplicating the song record. A setlist can hold ordered songs, edit controls, share/export access, and progress reset actions. Create a setlist Choose the personal or band library that should own the setlist. Open Sets and create a new setlist with a clear name. Add a performance date when the set is tied to an event. Use Add songs to choose charts from the selected library. Review the order before rehearsal and adjust it as the show changes. Use the Songs menu in Setlists to add or remove songs. Linked songs are automatically added when the main/parent song is added to the setlist. Slot details and notes Add slot notes for intros, cues, transitions, capo reminders, or leader notes. Reorder songs by long-pressing a song and dragging it to a new position. Add notes to songs in a setlist. Played / skipped Use the leftmost live-bar button to cycle the current setlist song through unplayed, played, and skipped. Mark songs as played/skipped in a setlist. Previous: PDFs Next: Live Performance

articles.title: Settings
articles.summary: Make Songivo your own with controls for your profile, song display, colors, metronome, editor, libraries, and more.
articles.content: Preferences Settings Songivo is fully customizable, so your songbook can feel at home in rehearsal, on stage, and everywhere in between. Songivo Settings Profile Personalize the details and controls you see most often. Your display name for song history and band attribution. The iPad top-bar title size. The floating control overlay’s size and transparency. Song and setlist numbering, plus song-list sectioning. iCloud Sync Keep your personal library in step across your devices. There is nothing to configure in Songivo: songs, setlists, tags, and themes sync automatically when iCloud is available. Use the status display to confirm that your library is up to date. Band Set up and manage the shared libraries your group uses. Create a band, join one from a shared link, or select the band you manage. Name a band, invite members, and manage membership. Share an invite link for collaborators. Song Shape how ChordPro songs read on the screen. Chord notation, layout mode, split-page threshold, and song-block alignment. Song-header and ChordPro-label size, spacing, and emphasis. Body text size and font family. Color Give your charts a look that is clear in any lighting. System, light, or dark appearance. Chord, lyric, background, verse, chorus, and bridge colors for light and dark themes. ChordPro label colors for light and dark themes. Metronome Make the metronome fit your playing environment. The beat-flash color. The metronome click sound. Song Editor Keep the editor focused on the information your library needs. Whether author, copyright, CCLI, and time-signature fields appear. Purchases Manage your Songivo plan and available band capacity. Choose a yearly unlimited-song subscription or a lifetime unlock for unlimited song additions and access to shared band libraries with more than 5 songs. Add active band slots when your group needs more room. Restore eligible purchases for your Apple Account. Backup & Restore Back up a library or restore it when you need to. Choose a personal or band library to export as a backup. Choose the destination library when restoring a backup. Documentation Find help whenever you need a refresher. Open the documentation or start the in-app tutorial. About Find the essentials about the app and where to get help. View app version information, contact support, or open the privacy policy. Previous: Exporting Next: Troubleshooting

articles.title: Song Library
articles.summary: Search, filter, open, link, copy, export, and manage songs in the Songivo library.
articles.content: Library Song Library The library is where Songivo keeps your charts searchable, filtered, and ready for setlists. Use the library panel to choose the active library context, find songs, and open the chart you want to rehearse or perform. Search, sort, library switching, and song selection stay in the panel so the chart can remain visible. Find songs quickly Search by title, artist, and available metadata. Sort the list when title, artist, key, or other metadata is the fastest way to find a chart. Use song numbers when your paper binder, rehearsal plan, or band workflow depends on numbered charts. Keep tags consistent so filtering remains useful as the library grows. Library actions at the bottom of the panel handle creation, importing, and exporting while the current chart stays open. Manage song records Open a song from the selected library. Use Edit Song to update title, artist, key, BPM, duration, tags, links, optional fields, and chart source. In a shared band, favorite the linked version you personally perform. Duplicate a song when you need a separate arrangement rather than overwriting the original. Delete only from the library where the song should be removed. Song history Review up to five previous versions of a song and restore the version you need. Choose a previous version, review its changes, then select Restore This Version. Browse a song’s version history and restore a previous version. Copy between libraries Copy songs between My Library and band libraries only when you intentionally want separate records. Songivo keeps personal and band material independent, so changes in one library do not silently rewrite the other. If Songivo finds a duplicate title during copy or import, review the prompt before creating another copy. Previous: Getting Started Next: Link Songs

articles.title: Swiping
articles.summary: Use Songivo swipe gestures to move between songs and reveal row actions in the song library.
articles.content: Gestures Swiping Songivo uses swipe gestures in several places to help you move through songs and reveal actions. Swipe between songs On multi-page ChordPro or PDF songs, swipe left or right to turn chart pages. At the first or last page of an active setlist song, swiping can continue to the previous or next available setlist song. Swipe right on the song viewer to move back to the previous available setlist song. Swipe left or right on a song. Swipe song rows In the song library, row swipes reveal management actions for that song. Swipe from the leading edge for actions such as Link and Copy to Library. For a linked song in a shared band, Favorite selects the version you perform. Swipe from the trailing edge when you intend to delete a song. Swipe right on a song in the menu to reveal actions. Swipe left on a song to delete. Swipe setlist overview rows In the setlist library, row swipes reveal management actions for that setlist. Swipe from the leading edge for actions such as Rename and Duplicate. Swipe from the trailing edge when you intend to delete the setlist. Swipe right on a setlist in the menu to reveal actions. Swipe left on a setlist to delete. Swipe setlist song rows After selecting a setlist, row swipes reveal management actions for that song in a setlist. Swipe from the leading edge for adding notes. Swipe from the trailing edge when you intend to delete the song from that setlist. Swipe right on a setlist song in the menu to reveal actions. Swipe left on a setlist song to delete. When swipes do nothing If no previous or next song is available, Songivo stays on the current song. If annotation mode is active, tap Done before using song navigation swipes. If the song list is open, swipe the row rather than the main chart area when you want row actions. If you are zoomed into a PDF, confirm whether the gesture is moving the page rather than the setlist. Previous: Tuner & Metronome Next: Annotations

articles.title: Troubleshooting
articles.summary: Troubleshoot Songivo import, PDF, ChordPro, setlist, live mode, sync, band, tuner, and export issues.
articles.content: Fixes Troubleshooting When something looks wrong, first confirm where you are: My Library or a band library, song or setlist, ChordPro or PDF, viewer or editor. Import does not look right Confirm the file type is supported: ChordPro, plain text, PDF, image, or SongBook Pro. For PDFs, revisit the preview step and check rotation, crop, perspective, and contrast. For text charts, inspect whether the source needs ChordPro cleanup after import. Check duplicate prompts before assuming the import failed. Sync is behind Confirm the device is online. Confirm iCloud is available for the Apple ID on the device. Check whether you are viewing My Library or a band library. Use the sync button. Open Settings to get more details. Contact support with diagnostics if the same issue repeats. Band changes do not appear Check that the correct band library is selected. Confirm the member has accepted the band invite. Run band sync and review band sync health. Resolve any Conflict needs review items. Confirm the missing song was copied into the band library instead of remaining only in My Library. Tuner cannot hear input Confirm microphone permission in iOS Settings and make sure another app is not holding the microphone. The tuner uses microphone input for pitch detection and does not store audio. When contacting support Include your device model, iOS or iPadOS version, Songivo version, what you expected, what happened, and screenshots or diagnostics if available. Previous: Settings Next: FAQ

articles.title: Tuner & Metronome
articles.summary: Use Songivo tuner and metronome tools from the song workflow, including microphone permission and metronome settings.
articles.content: Stage tools Tuner & Metronome The tuner and metronome are quick performance tools you can open without leaving the song workflow. Use the tuner Open a song. Choose the tuner action from the command bar (top right). Allow microphone access when asked. Play one note at a time and watch the pitch feedback. Close the tuner when you are ready to return to the chart. The tuner opens over the chart, so you can check tuning and return to the song without changing context. Use the metronome Short tap starts or stops the metronome. Long press opens Tap Tempo. Tap repeatedly in the BPM area to set the tempo; tap outside it to close. Adjust metronome sound in Settings when another click tone is easier to hear. Tap repeatedly into the BPM area to set the tempo. Microphone privacy The tuner uses microphone input only for pitch detection. Songivo does not record, store, or transmit tuner audio. Previous: Live Performance Next: Swiping
